claims.statement: ATO lists a single version separately and describes a single edit in the June 2022 release.

assessment.rationale: Primary label names the edit; audio match remains open.

claims.statement: Will Turner is credited as composer, producer and mixer on the 4:03 Miles And Miles.

assessment.rationale: Cannot inherit edit or mastering responsibilities without single-specific evidence.

claims.statement: The EP recordings were made in a London flat.

assessment.rationale: Direct participant statements; not an identified commercial studio.

claims.statement: Turner describes deliberately working with eight tracks and both old and new gear.

assessment.rationale: Does not identify tape format or machine.

claims.statement: Turner previously played in The White Feather Collective.

assessment.rationale: Earlier band connection, not a shared session credit.

claims.statement: Turner grew up in Malvern; Fuller grew up near Brighton.

assessment.rationale: Origin, band base and recording location must remain distinct.

claims.statement: Turner connects Miles and Miles to imagined American travel.

assessment.rationale: Author's account of inspiration, not an audible finding.

claims.statement: The expanded EP covers Real Love Baby, Desert Raven and Guinnevere.

assessment.rationale: Cover relationship is not artist collaboration.

claims.statement: Turner names Princeton/Marshall amplification, a 1981 Les Paul Standard and Danelectro spring reverb while discussing One of a Kind.

assessment.rationale: Cannot attach this rig to the seed track.

claims.statement: The later expansion to five members does not establish all five played on the original EP.

assessment.rationale: Conservative interpretation; full track roster unresolved.

claims.statement: Rogers and Ian Fitchuk wrote and produced the single, written March 2023 and released October 8 2024.
claims.locator: release text and artist credit block

assessment.rationale: Artist and label accounts may share announcement provenance.

claims.statement: The artist credits Konrad Snyder for engineering, Fitchuk and Sam Evian for instrumentation, Jonathan Low for mixing and Emily Lazar for mastering.

assessment.rationale: Artist's own explicit roles.

claims.statement: AllMusic assigns bass, drums, acoustic/electric guitar and keyboards to Fitchuk; electric guitar and engineering to Evian.

assessment.rationale: Granular roles exceed the artist post; retain secondary attribution.

claims.statement: AllMusic lists Lauren Marquez and Michael Deano as assistant engineers.

assessment.rationale: Original detailed liner credits not yet obtained.

claims.statement: Electric Lady is documented for the early Don't Forget Me sessions.

assessment.rationale: Does not explicitly establish the March single's room.

claims.statement: Rogers' attraction to Fitchuk's work on Kacey Musgraves' Golden Hour is described in her album interview.

assessment.rationale: Not a claimed specific song template.

claims.statement: Evian performed as Sam Owens in Celestial Shore and worked at Figure 8 Recording before his Catskills studio.

assessment.rationale: Biographical content in a participant interview, not Maggie session location.

claims.statement: Evian cites Glyn Johns and the Get Back sessions as inspiration for Plunge's workflow.

assessment.rationale: Direct self-attributed influence, not inferred resemblance.

claims.statement: Evian describes live room recording without click/headphones and early takes for Plunge.

assessment.rationale: Do not transfer this method to In the Living Room.

claims.statement: The Plunge interview identifies a Warmoth-based custom guitar, Lollar gold-foil pickups, Cali76, Tumnus, Warped Vinyl, Twilighter and M 160 into a Neve preamp.

assessment.rationale: Pedal order, settings and Neve model not established.

claims.statement: Evian describes recording Plunge on a Tascam 48 and transferring to an MCI 16-track two-inch machine.

assessment.rationale: MCI model not specified; not Maggie track evidence.

claims.statement: The Plunge interviews identify a collaborator circle including Adrianne Lenker, El Kempner and Liam Kazar.

assessment.rationale: Does not establish those musicians on the Maggie single.

claims.statement: The label biography establishes Maryland as Rogers' origin.

assessment.rationale: No exact hometown established in this pass.

claims.statement: Running Around is listed as track 14, duration 2:34, with a July 19 2024 album release and RCA/mcDJ rights line.

assessment.rationale: Not a file-level master match.

claims.statement: Producer credits name Donald Glover, Michael Uzowuru, Riley Mackin, Tyler Johnson and Willow Smith.
claims.locator: track 14 credits; artist release producer field

assessment.rationale: Both distributors may have common upstream metadata.

claims.statement: Riley Mackin, Tyler Johnson and Emi Trevena are credited on guitar; Aaron Steele on drums.

assessment.rationale: Instrument roles known; models, part assignment and session location unknown.

claims.statement: Fousheé is the featured artist and Willow Smith is credited for background vocal.

assessment.rationale: Featured vs background roles preserved.

claims.statement: Riley Mackin, Brittney Orinda and Zachary Brown receive recording-engineer credits.

assessment.rationale: No implication they worked together in one room.

claims.statement: Stuart White is credited with mixing and Colin Leonard with mastering.

assessment.rationale: Studio/console/effects not provided.

claims.statement: Patrick Gardner, Conner McFarland and Matheus Braz receive assistant-engineer credits.

assessment.rationale: Retain distributor spelling; AllMusic search result differed on Conner/Connor.

claims.statement: Steele's portfolio lists collaborations across several artists and includes Simmer and Sudden Desire as demos.

assessment.rationale: Demo listing is a branch candidate, not full verified song-role documentation.

claims.statement: The Trap Set's episode summary describes Steele's New York upbringing and Bill Withers/At the Drive-In background.

assessment.rationale: Publisher summary, not a podcast listened to in this run; not track inspiration.

claims.statement: White's original interview explains mixes from the album using Hearts Were Meant to Fly and We Are God as named examples.

assessment.rationale: No explicit Running Around breakdown identified. Automatic names not validated by listening.

claims.statement: Turner's EP constraint and Evian's Plunge process suggest comparing deliberate recording limitations.

assessment.rationale: No direct historical link, shared machine or sonic match established.

claims.statement: Headline band/solo categories do not describe the full recording team.

assessment.rationale: Explains research design; gender is not treated as a sonic cause.

claims.statement: No shared producer, room or gear has been established across all three seeds in this search set.

assessment.rationale: Not proof that no connection exists.
